setup.description: Create a feature branch on the DataCopilot repo (213) for eval runs. Pass the branch ID to each eval prompt.
setup.command: dxs source branch create --repo 213 --title "grid-creator-eval-{timestamp}" --description "Temporary branch for grid-creator skill evals"

evals.name: new-odata-grid-owned-datasource
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create a grid that lists our warehouses — columns for the warehouse name, the type name, and the created date. Nothing else will ever consume this data; it exists only to feed this grid. Reference name: eval_warehouses_grid.
evals.expected_output: A validated and upserted OData-backed grid with an owned embedded datasource (isOwned: true), correct queryOptions.selects coverage, full component-identity envelope, build-required pageSize/columnSizingType, coerced text bindings, and a grid-validator pass.
expectations: The transcript shows the pre-author rows-source decision: schema exploration (dxs schema search / dxs schema describe-entity or the schema-explorer agent) confirming the Warehouses entity BEFORE the grid body was authored — the agent did not default to a flow-type datasource for an obvious OData entity

The datasource is authored as an OWNED entry embedded in the grid's datasources[] array with datasourceConfig.isOwned: true — the transcript does NOT create a standalone datasource config (no separate 'dxs configuration upsert datasource') for this grid-only source

The embedded datasource has type 'oDataQuery' with getListFlow and getByKeysFlow null (the OData variant), and every column-bound field appears in datasources[0].queryOptions.selects (nested fields such as the type name in the appropriate expands[].queryOptions.selects) — the runtime-only location that actually retrieves the data

The entity fields appear in the applicable type-metadata locations: datasources[0].queryOptionsObjectTypeDef, datasources[0].outParams[result].objectTypeDef, and datasourceConfig.configOutParameters[result].objectTypeDef

pageSize is present as a concrete integer (e.g. 25) and columnSizingType is a valid camelCase member ('cellsWidth' / 'headersWidth' / 'fixedWidth' / 'fitedWidth') — neither is null or omitted (both are build-required: the grid imports without them and then fails the build)

The embedded datasource carries the full component-identity envelope: datasources[0].referenceName exactly equals datasourceConfig.configId, plus title, non-empty description ≤ 100 chars, hasKey: true, hasResult: true, and accessModifier 'private'

Non-string column bindings are coerced at the bind site (created date via $utils.date.format(...) or equivalent; any numeric field via ?.toString() or a template literal) — the entity schema's declared types are NOT changed to string to satisfy display bindings
The grid's referenceName is eval_warehouses_grid (snake_case, _grid suffix) and its description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains a 'dxs configuration validate grid' command run before 'dxs configuration upsert grid'
After authoring, the transcript shows a grid-validator invocation (the mandatory grid-specific gate) — not merely the generic component-validator

evals.name: new-flow-grid-aggregated-rows
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: I want a grid eval_pick_velocity_grid that shows picks-per-day aggregated per warehouse — columns for warehouse name, pick date, and pick count. There is no single entity for this; the rows are computed by combining task data. Build the grid with whatever datasource type fits.
evals.expected_output: A flow-type embedded grid datasource (getListFlow/getByKeysFlow populated) with all five entity-shape locations in sync, $top/$skip pagination, matching key defs, all-or-nothing filter state, validated, upserted, and grid-validator-checked.
expectations: The embedded datasource is flow-type (type: 'flows') with getListFlow and getByKeysFlow both populated (paginated shape), resultIsCollection: true, hasKey: true, hasResult: true — the agent recognized the computed/aggregated rowset as flow-type work rather than forcing an OData query

The row shape appears identically in all five entity-shape locations: datasources[0].queryOptionsObjectTypeDef, datasources[0].outParams[result].objectTypeDef, getListFlow.outParams[result].objectTypeDef, getByKeysFlow.outParams[result].objectTypeDef, and datasourceConfig.configOutParameters[result].objectTypeDef
$top and $skip are declared on getListFlow.inParams (normal pagination inputs), and the getListFlow code sets $flow.outParams.totalCount alongside $flow.outParams.result
keyDef on the embedded datasource and datasourceConfig.datasourceKeyDef agree (same ids and types)

Dynamic filter/sort is in an all-or-nothing state: either no dynamicFilters/dynamicOrderBys registrations at all, or registrations + per-column wiring + application inside getListFlow code — never the half-wired state where UI controls are registered but the flow ignores $filter/$orderby
No $filter or $orderby entries are manually declared in any inParams list (datasources[0].inParams, getListFlow.inParams, getByKeysFlow.inParams) or in datasourceConfig.configParameters
pageSize is present as an integer and columnSizingType is a valid camelCase member; the referenceName is eval_pick_velocity_grid ending in _grid; the description is non-empty and ≤ 100 characters
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate grid' run before 'dxs configuration upsert grid'
After authoring, the transcript shows a grid-validator invocation (the mandatory gate after every grid edit)

evals.name: add-dynamic-filter-five-locations
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: the grid eval_pick_velocity_grid should exist on the branch (if it does not, first create it: a flow-type embedded datasource whose row shape is { warehouse_name: string, pick_date: string, pick_count: number }, with columns for all three). Then make the warehouse name column filterable and sortable from its column header.
evals.expected_output: A dynamic filter added per the full grids.md checklist: field in all five entity-shape locations, identical registrations in both registration sites, four per-column wiring fields, no manual $filter/$orderby declarations, and getListFlow actually applying the inputs (state A).
expectations: warehouse_name is present in all five entity-shape locations after the edit (datasources[0].queryOptionsObjectTypeDef, datasources[0].outParams[result].objectTypeDef, getListFlow.outParams[result].objectTypeDef, getByKeysFlow.outParams[result].objectTypeDef, datasourceConfig.configOutParameters[result].objectTypeDef) — verifiable by grepping a neighbor field id and comparing occurrence counts

The field is registered in BOTH registration sites with identical entries: datasources[0].dynamicFilters AND datasourceConfig.dynamicFilters (and likewise in both dynamicOrderBys lists for sorting) — no drift between the embedded-datasource side and the consumer side
The warehouse name column carries all four per-column wiring fields: dynamicFilter, dynamicOrderBy, dynamicFilterType (inParam-shaped leaf type), and dynamicFilterControl (textBox for a string field)

No $filter or $orderby entry was added to any inParams list (datasources[0].inParams, getListFlow.inParams, getByKeysFlow.inParams) or to datasourceConfig.configParameters — the platform auto-injects typed versions from the registrations and manual entries collide

getListFlow code applies both inputs to the row set (the canonical applyDynamicFilter / applyDynamicOrderBy helpers or equivalent, reading ($flow.inParams as any).$filter and ($flow.inParams as any).$orderby) — the edit does not leave the half-wired bug state where filter UI is registered but the data never responds

If the grid already existed on the branch, the modification used the corrected round-trip: 'dxs configuration get grid ... -O envelope.json', then extraction of the inner .json (jq .json envelope.json or equivalent) before editing — the envelope was never piped directly back into upsert
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate grid' run before the final 'dxs configuration upsert grid'
After the edit, the transcript shows a grid-validator invocation (mandatory after every grid edit, including filter/sort registration changes)
The grid's description remains non-empty and at most 100 characters

evals.name: toolbar-button-and-row-flow
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: on eval_pick_velocity_grid (if it is not on the branch, first create it: flow-type embedded datasource, row shape { warehouse_name: string, pick_date: string, pick_count: number }), add a 'Delete selected' toolbar button that must only be clickable when rows are selected, and add per-row behavior that runs when each row's data loads and writes a 'No picks' note into a status cell for rows whose pick count is zero.
evals.expected_output: A destructive selection-gated toolbar button with the click handler inside buttonConfig, plus a $row-reading flow correctly registered in rowFlows[], imperatively-populated status cell left with an empty declarative binding, validated and grid-validator-checked.
expectations: The per-row flow (the one whose body reads the $row global) is registered in rowFlows[], NOT in flows[] — pointing onRowDataLoadedFlowConfig at the flow is not sufficient on its own; the flow object itself must live in rowFlows[]
The toolbar button's click handler lives INSIDE the type-specific config block (buttonConfig.clickFlowConfig.flowId) — not at the toolbar entry's top level
The toolbar entry has type 'button' and its sibling *Config blocks are present and explicitly null (matching the platform convention), with the click flow declared in the grid's flows[]
The destructive delete button carries buttonDefaultStyleClass: 'destructive' inside its buttonConfig

The selection-gated button seeds readOnly: true statically in buttonConfig AND an on_select_row flow toggles its readOnly live (e.g. from the current selection / $grid.selectedRows) — both halves present, so the button mounts disabled before the first selection event
The status column written imperatively keeps an empty declarative displayControl value (e.g. "") — it is NOT bound to $row.entity.<field> for a field the entity does not carry
Every $grid.vars.<id> or $row.vars.<id> written in the new flow code is declared in the grid's top-level vars[] / rowVars[] arrays
If the grid already existed, the modification used the corrected round-trip (dxs configuration get grid -O envelope.json, then jq .json extraction before editing)
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate grid' run before 'dxs configuration upsert grid'
After the edit, the transcript shows a grid-validator invocation

evals.name: cell-styling-two-targets
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: on eval_pick_velocity_grid (if missing, first create it: flow-type embedded datasource, row shape { warehouse_name: string, pick_date: string, pick_count: number }), style the rows: when pick count is 0 the pick count cell should get an attention-style background; the warehouse name cell should look clickable (pointer cursor and underline on hover); and zero-pick rows should show a warning icon in a cell.
evals.expected_output: Cell styling done through the correct APIs: setAttentionClass on ICellStyles for the background, hover/cursor styling on displayControl.styles (the inner control), no .icon on a text-typed cell, and correct flow registration — validated and grid-validator-checked.
expectations: The attention background uses $row.cells.<col>.styles.setAttentionClass() — the only class toggle ICellStyles exposes. The code does NOT call setDestructiveClass / setPlannedClass / setCreationClass / setClass on a grid cell (those exist only on button styles, not on cells)

Cursor / hover / text-decoration styling is applied via $row.cells.<col>.displayControl.styles.setStyle(...) (the inner control element) — NOT via $row.cells.<col>.styles.setStyle(...) (the parent cell div), where control-level properties type-check but have zero visible effect

No .icon is assigned to a text-typed cell's displayControl (ITextModel has no .icon): either the icon-bearing column's displayControl.type is changed to 'button' before assigning displayControl.icon, or the warning is carried another way (e.g. in cell text) with the ITextModel constraint acknowledged in the transcript
Every flow whose body references the $row global is registered in rowFlows[]; styling implemented by iterating $grid.rows inside on_data_loaded may legitimately live in flows[]
If the grid already existed, the modification used the corrected round-trip (dxs configuration get grid -O envelope.json, then jq .json extraction before editing)
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate grid' run before 'dxs configuration upsert grid'
After the edit, the transcript shows a grid-validator invocation

evals.name: full-text-search-wiring
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: eval_warehouses_grid (the OData-backed warehouses grid — if it is not on the branch, first create it with an owned OData datasource over Warehouses showing name, type name, and created date) needs the built-in search box so users can search warehouses by name. Wire it up end to end so typing in the box actually filters the rows.
evals.expected_output: fullTextSearch: true with an explicit configParameters entry valued $grid.fullTextSearch, a full_text_search inParam declared on the embedded OData datasource, and a conditional OData filter reading $datasource.inParams.full_text_search — validated and grid-validator-checked.
expectations: fullTextSearch is set to the bare boolean true — not null and not an object like { "enabled": true } (both shapes fail import; the server expects a bare System.Boolean)
The embedded OData datasource declares a full_text_search inParam

datasourceConfig.configParameters contains an EXPLICIT entry whose parameter id is full_text_search and whose value is "$grid.fullTextSearch" — the wiring does not rely on auto-forwarding from the search box (there is none)

The OData datasource's filter expression reads the value via $datasource.inParams.full_text_search (the OData-variant access path — not $flow.inParams.full_text_search, which is the flow-datasource path)
The search filter is applied conditionally — when the search value is undefined/empty the base query still returns unfiltered rows (the conditional filter pattern)
If the grid already existed, the modification used the corrected round-trip (dxs configuration get grid -O envelope.json, then jq .json extraction before editing)
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate grid' run before 'dxs configuration upsert grid'
After the edit, the transcript shows a grid-validator invocation
